ceiling.why_machine_readable: The value was free prose and no tool under tools/ read the key, while `seeds` and `allocation` — its machine-readable siblings — are both consumed and gated. CLAUDE.md makes the credit ceiling a per-spec obligation and records that spent credits have no compensator, so the one unrecoverable resource in this repo was bounded by a string nothing could parse. The prose is not deleted: it is `note`, verbatim, and the number a submission step can count against sits beside it. CORRECTION, 2026-09-04 (swarm wave 8, F-6c5c537b). This paragraph used to argue the fix with the clause “while `seeds` and `allocation` — its machine-readable siblings — are both consumed and gated”, and to close “and the number a submission step can count against sits beside it”. Both halves were measured on the tree and only one survived. `grep -rn allocation tools/ --include=*.py` returns 0 hits: `allocation` has no reader at all, so it is exactly as unread as `ceiling` was when it was filed. `seeds` has seven readers — build_animate_payload.py:484 (main), build_camera_i2v_payload.py:1179 (main), build_i2v_payload.py:790 (main), build_lora_arm_payload.py:466 (gate_s), build_r2v_payload.py:323 (build_and_write), build_t2v_payload.py:498 (main) and gate_saved_graph.py:892 (main) — each handing the list to a seed gate, so that half of the claim holds. And no tool reads `ceiling` from a seeds spec either: every `ceiling` hit under tools/ is `armature_core.assembly`'s unrelated CASCADE slot ceiling, or a builder passing that one. So `ceiling.submissions` is a number a submission step COULD count against and none does today — the bound is held by the spec and the executor, not by code. The original claim is kept above rather than deleted, because the correction is more useful than the original. tests/test_seeds_specs.py pins the measurement; the day a builder counts against `ceiling.submissions`, that test flips with it and this paragraph is rewritten again. RE-ANCHORED, 2026-09-04 (swarm wave 14). Three of the seven citations moved because gates were added above their readers, and the line numbers were RE-MEASURED rather than re-typed: build_i2v_payload.py 620 -> 687 (start_image_record gained the fit_disagrees_with_the_file andon, F-e17613c2), build_r2v_payload.py 217 -> 272 (Gate CEILING gained its behaviour-keyed hosted-node census, F-eec3f145), and gate_saved_graph.py 487 -> 602 (route_facts reads the two facts Gate ROUTE needs off the builder's payload record, F-2da88c51). The other four are unmoved. The function name beside each number is the anchor that survives the next move; tests/test_seeds_specs.py checks the pair, which is how this drift was found. why_a_new_list_rather_than_the_old_reser: specs/E09-seeds.json registered 20260811 (spent on the probe) and 20260812 (its reserve). Reusing 20260812 here would put a seed registered for one trajectory onto a different one, and the record would then have to explain which run a number belonged to. A same-seed re-roll against the probe was considered and rejected on the measurement, not on tidiness: the prompt changes in this run too, so an identical noise draw would isolate nothing, and the two trajectories diverge from step 0 anyway (different shift, different step count).
binds_in_both_directions: An experiment that pre-registered seeds must use one of them, and an experiment that pre-registered none may not vary its seed at all. tools/armature_core/route_gates.py::gate_s_registration enforces both clauses in code against the graph that is about to run, and ignores the inert seed of an add_noise=disable sampler because demanding registration there would be a check that fires on a correct two-expert split.
